fatal_flaws: The headline effect is not robust: p=0.213 after the search, held-out gain CI [-10.0, 17.7], the plus group beats forecast only 50% of the time, and one player carries half the slope.

judge-football.justification:
Usable 7.9: The decision card names four 2025 players with a stated rule, a per-player call and a film cue, and it includes a drill-protocol ask (record Hoop G, run the hoop twice, make every DL run the 3-cone). The call is only a tie-break worth about 0.6 pressures a season. The held-out lift is not distinguishable from zero, and the clean-class plus calls went 0 of 2, so a GM would treat it as a lead and not act on it.

Difficulty 8.7: It handles most of the hard parts: noise-corrected single-run reliability (0.41), a forecast that prices pick, weight, role and NGS score, the held-out class, multiple screening (best of 14, p=0.12), and the 20-rush game samples that carry no blockers or scheme. It also separates weight from Hoop G for interior DL and separates EDGE from interior calls. It does not address drill-protocol changes across years beyond the within-year standardization, and rotation and injuries are mentioned only as limitations.

Unique 7.6: Translating a Combine tracking drill (Run-the-Hoop lateral g) into a pass-rush tiebreak for players who skipped the 3-cone is not another 'does the 40 predict' regression. The drill-to-game link is null (0.07), so the core mechanism is unproven, and the 3-cone beats it where both exist.

Terminology 7.8: Terms are mostly sound: EDGE and interior, pressure rate, day-3, UDFA, stunts, 3-cone, and named players with picks. The 'how hard a lineman can lean into a turn' gloss, with 0.62 g mapped to a 1.8-yd radius, is physically concrete. Weak spots are the stats-heavy middle (exact intervals, log score, nested shuffle), and 'pick 100 vs 80' as a unit for 0.6 pressures is odd. The Phillips row reads 'No call' while its Hoop G interval is below zero, which is a labeling tension.
top_changes: Cut the statistical scaffolding from the middle of the piece. That means the log-score deltas, the 'where it does not apply' paragraph, the nested shuffle and the 14-pair multiplicity detail. Move them to one limitations line. Replace them with a plain 'if you are a DL coach/scout' paragraph and a raw plus-call vs no-call pressure-rate table split by EDGE and interior, with n beside each rate.

Make the decision card actionable for the 2026 Combine class, or at least state a forward-testable pre-registered rule. Add 3-4 more named prospects with a call each, including at least one minus-flag and one 'film first' call. Tie the calls to a specific draft-slot swap, for example 'prefer X over Y at pick N'. Resolve the Phillips tension: his interval is below zero but the call is 'no call', so label it explicitly as a film flag.

Reframe the lede and structure around the one result that is solid, and stop leading with a hoop number that is null out of class and null against in-game lateral g. The solid result is that the 3-cone predicts pressure and Hoop G is a stand-in for it where the 3-cone is missing. Put the protocol ask (everyone runs the 3-cone, record Hoop G, two hoop runs) up top as the main action. Then show one Figure 1 pair of traces on a shared time axis for a plus-call EDGE and a no-call interior, so a position coach can see what the number looks like.

judge-datascience.justification:
I re-ran checks from board_2023_2025.csv and the parquet-derived outputs. I did not re-run the full 2,154-line analysis.py, so the headline model numbers (0.6 pressures [-0.4, 1.7], +1.3 points R², p=0.01) are unverified. The board and calibration numbers all reproduce.

Correctness: The plus-call count is now consistent. The CSV has 10 plus calls, and the text scores 9 because Downs has only 7 rushes. The 2025 card figures match the CSV (Downs, Brinson, Ezeiruaku, Phillips). The 36% of the 2025 DL class with a 3-cone is 15 of 42. The grouped rates reproduce: 4/7 and 0/2 plus calls, 6/32 and 3/37 no-call. The Clopper-Pearson intervals match exactly (23-87, 0-78, 8-34, 2-20, 17-75). Two things are unclear. The 19% matched baseline for no-call rushers is not simple to reproduce: the raw pooled no-call hit rate is 9/69 = 13%, and the 19% rests on a role- and class-matched calculation I could not check. The permutation p is reported three ways (0.05 for the plus-call gap, 0.01 for the nested R² shuffle, 0.12 for best-of-14 multiplicity). All are disclosed, but a reader will find three p-values confusing.

Evidence: Strong. It states n per claim and uses exact binomial intervals. It separates the classes that tuned the rule from the clean 2025 class (0 of 2). The no-tracking baseline uses pick, weight, NGS and official times, with a complete-case version that has no imputation. Out-of-class validation is leave-one-class-out with 90% intervals and a log score. The multiplicity adjustment over 14 screened pairs and a power estimate are included. The honest finding is that the out-of-class gain is +1.3 points and the interval spans zero. The headline interval also spans zero (-0.4 to 1.7), and the 80% pick-equivalent range of 47-106 is very wide.

Model: Appropriate to n. It uses a beta-binomial mixed model with skeptical shrinkage, reliability correction (0.41 single-run, noise-corrected Hoop G), ridge as a prior-free check, year standardization, and a nested shuffle control. Slight over-engineering: 2,000+ lines for a null-ish result, and some cuts are very small (n=22, n=34).

Innovation: A new 10 Hz-derived metric (peak half-second lateral acceleration in Run-the-Hoop). It has a physical interpretation (0.62 g at 3.5 yd/s gives a turning radius of about 1.8 yd). It also includes a within-player check against in-game lateral g (null, ICC 0.03) and a drill-protocol recommendation. It does not yet include a drill-to-play matched movement-similarity metric.
top_changes: Add a single summary table of all p-values and intervals (shuffle p=0.05 vs 0.01 vs multiplicity 0.12) stating which null each tests. Show how the matched 19% no-call baseline is computed (role- and class-matched, with n), because the raw pooled no-call rate is 13%.

Add a pre-specified leave-one-class-out calibration of the call rule on the observed-times-only baseline, with rush-weighted exact intervals. Report the 2025 clean-test result as a posterior predictive probability of 0 of 2 under the shrunk effect. Also report the hit rate with Downs (7 rushes) excluded and included.

Strengthen the mechanism link. Match each hoop run to the same player's NFL rushes using a self-referenced peak lateral g percentile within speed bins, and test it separately for EDGE and interior with a player random effect. Alternatively, drop the drill-to-NFL claim to a single sentence.

judge-writeup.justification: check.py passes: 1,519 words, 3 figures, 2 tables, no problems. The title now states the finding and the audience (DL who skip the 3-cone). The lede gives the result, the unit and the caveat in about 70 words. The structure is close to the finalist pattern: a decision card up front, a one-sentence metric definition, held-out results with named players, and a limitations section. The piece is shorter and more actionable than earlier rounds. Weaknesses remain. (1) Motivation is thin: nothing says why pass-rush, why Run-the-Hoop, or why this Combine class. (2) Statistical scaffolding still dominates the second half: log scores, exact intervals, adjusted correlations, a nested shuffle, and 14-pair multiplicity. A scout cannot repeat that. (3) The headline "usable tiebreak" is partly contradicted by the body. The 4 hits are in-sample, the clean 2025 test went 0 of 2, the held-out intervals include zero, and the Sundays section finds nothing. The lede and the closing sections therefore pull against each other. (4) The Figure 1 caption describes a hero but the surrounding text is bullets. Figure 2 is numbered after Figure 3. (5) The lede's "gap between pick 100 and pick 80" comes late and is unexplained. (6) The text reports p=0.05 for the shuffle in one place and p=0.01 in the limitations. (7) The drill-protocol recommendation is useful for a team but is buried under the Sundays section. Tone is mostly confident and specific. It is still defensive in the second half.
top_changes: Add a 2-3 sentence motivation paragraph right after the lede, under a heading like 'Why linemen who skip the 3-cone'. It should say why pass-rush value is scarce, that only 36% of the 2025 DL class ran the 3-cone, and why the hoop is the only Combine drill with a lateral-force read. Also fix the lede, which promises a 'usable tiebreak' while the body shows the clean 2025 test went 0 of 2. Say 'a lead worth a film check, not a rule' instead.

Cut the stats-heavy middle: collapse the 'Where the tiebreak applies', 'Where it does not' and 'How the headline is built' paragraphs into one 3-row table (no-3-cone n=56, with-3-cone n=34, all-measure n=22) with one-line takeaways. Move log scores, the 14-pair shrinkage and the 840-rusher power note to the notebook or appendix. Pointing to an appendix would also satisfy the finalist pattern.

Reconcile the inconsistent numbers and ordering. Fix the shuffle p (p=0.05 in the results section vs p=0.01 in the limitations) and renumber the figures in order of appearance (Figure 2 appears after Figure 3). Move the drill-protocol recommendation up as the 'so-what for a team' section ahead of the Sundays negative result. Shorten the Sundays section to its three key numbers.

judge-viz.justification: Three figures plus 2 tables, which is well under the cap of 9. Fig 1 is a strong tracking-native hero: hoop path colored by lateral g, drill and NFL traces on one peak-aligned time axis, and the pressure rate against a no-tracking forecast with an interval. The bottom scatter answers its own question honestly: the drill does not show up after weight and role. Fig 3 is a small-multiples player card with sparklines, forecast ticks, intervals, exact binomial bars, and the tuning classes separated from clean 2025. Accuracy is good. Axes start at 0, n is stated per row, intervals are shown, and the tuned-versus-clean split is labeled. Weaknesses are as follows. (1) Fig 2 is a dot-and-whisker chart. It is dense, its labels overlap ('-3.1' and '+1.3' sit on the grey strip, and the 'shuffled Hoop G' label collides with the strip). The -73.3 arrow is truncated, which hides the scale, and it mixes correlation and R-squared panels, so it carries two messages. (2) Fig 3 has large dead whitespace under the header and above the 2025 block. It has a crowded footer legend, and its sparklines have no shared x-axis label. Fig 3 also repeats Fig 1's Solomon, Ezeiruaku, Adebawore and Brinson. The 2025 binomial bar (0 of 2, 0-78%) is nearly uninformative and costs a lot of space. (3) Fig 1 is very tall at 1240x2000, so at Kaggle column width the subtitle and in-panel text shrink toward about 8 pt. The four rows are repetitive. The lower scatter's annotation text is a prose block that belongs in the caption. The figure order in the text is 1, 3, 2, which is odd. The bottom scatter's hoop-speed metric is hard to parse.
top_changes: Fig 1: cut it to a three-row hero (best EDGE hit, the clean 2025 miss, the low interior flag) and drop the Adebawore row. Move the bottom scatter into its own small panel, or into Fig 2 as panel (a). Put the 'how to read it' prose in the caption. Shrink the figure height so text stays at 9 pt or larger at column width. Add a shared x-axis label to the sparklines.

Fig 2: split it into one message. Keep panel (b), the held-out-class R-squared gain, and drop or merge the correlation panel (a) into a 3-row table. Fix the label collisions with the grey strip. Replace the -73.3 arrow with a broken-axis marker plus a note, or clip the axis explicitly. Renumber so the figures appear in the order 1, 2, 3 in the text.

Fig 3: remove the dead whitespace, put the group bars in one compact column (or a table row), and use hollow markers for 2025 rows. Add a base-rate band for each group. Put the sparklines on a common labeled time axis, and drop the duplicate players already shown in Fig 1 to avoid repeating figures. Fold in the no-call groups as two summary rows so the plus-versus-no-call contrast is visible.
